_readme: Hand-authored per-issue art direction for the ChatGPT cover-prompt generator.
tools/prompts_chatgpt.py joins this with issues/table.json (titles, beats, palettes).
The series-level preamble, register definitions and closing constraints live in
tools/prompts_chatgpt.py so that identity is enforced in one place and cannot drift
per issue. The defect in the abandoned local-SD route was exactly this: identity was
baked into each issue file, so 4 issues shared one prompt.
register : A | B | C | D | E   (see .agents/skills/amph-cover-prompt/references/registers.md)
subject  : ONE concrete focal image. Never an abstraction, never a mood word.
geometry : the compositional trick from table.json `idea`, restated as an instruction.
text     : "none" (default, rule 7 of the canon) or an object {allow:[...]} naming the
exact strings to render, per the measured corpus finding that fake text is
prompt-driven: name the string and it complies, leave it vague and it
ground   : optional override for the register's background; the register block always states one.

1.subject: a single road that runs east and coils into an endless descending spiral of shrinking stone rings
1.geometry: concentric rings shrinking toward a low vanishing point so the eye falls down and inward; road stays horizontal across frame, never vertical

2.subject: a small hooded figure seen strictly from behind, mid-stride, climbing a stair that turns away from the viewer
2.geometry: figure occupies under a tenth of the frame, placed low and off-centre; the stair rakes diagonally up-right

3.subject: four ruined doorways nested one inside the next, receding into a tunnel of broken stone
3.geometry: concentric recession: four arches, each smaller and further in, so a flat image reads as deep space

4.subject: a heavy stone doorframe with exactly one opening, built from two unequal arcs that meet off-axis
4.geometry: two arcs, one opening; the portal refuses symmetry — no mirror line anywhere in the frame

5.subject: a single ordinary object — a plain chair — mirrored across a hard vertical seam so its two halves refuse to resolve
5.geometry: perfect bilateral mirror across the centre line; mirrored so hard the object stops being an object

6.subject: one tiny cloaked figure from behind at the bottom edge, reaching up toward a tower that fills the entire upper frame and goes out of view
6.geometry: a small figure wanting something enormous; scale contrast carries the whole story, detail only in the tower

7.subject: two storks facing each other across a hard vertical seam, one rendered in cold light and one in hot, each long beak open
7.geometry: the mirror must produce two subjects arguing, not a decorative pattern; the seam is a hard edge with no gradient

8.subject: an ornate symmetrical brain-like form split down the middle: the left half rendered entirely in cold cyan line-work, the right half entirely in hot magenta and orange, meeting at one hard vertical seam
8.geometry: the duotone split is the signature look of the series: one object, two colour temperatures, hard seam, perfect bilateral symmetry

9.subject: one large hand-built shape — a key — assembled entirely from hundreds of tiny identical machined keys
9.geometry: the macro form must be readable only at distance; zoom in and it dissolves into components

10.subject: a black-and-white comic page of six panels where a figure walks east through all six, the drawing confident and the lettering a row of meaningless glyph shapes
10.geometry: a real panel grid with real gutters and screentone; the drawing is right and the words are wrong

11.subject: a spinal column of interlocking vertebrae that spirals upward and outward, each vertebra lit from within
11.geometry: bones assembled along a rising spiral so the column reads as something being manufactured, not anatomically posed

12.subject: eight identical standing glyph-figures in a ring, each one a closed shape with a single piece cut out of it
12.geometry: eight of the same thing in one colour reads as holy stillness; perfect radial repetition, no variation

13.subject: a glyph-form with exactly three wings, mid-beat, wings at one-twentieth past full extension
13.geometry: exactly three repetitions of the wing shape, spaced 120 degrees apart, so it reads as motion rather than pattern

14.subject: a hub-and-spoke chart so dense the labels collide and the outer ring breaks into illegible noise
14.geometry: this image is a warning, not a style: deliberately over-dense, unreadable at thumbnail size

15.subject: a beam of pale wine-red light crossing the frame corner to corner, striking a standing glyph-form at its exact centre
15.geometry: one diagonal of light crossing the whole frame makes the image alive; the glyph is the only thing the beam touches

16.subject: two robed figures facing each other, both bent forward in reverence, one holding the other at the chest
16.geometry: reverence drawn as two bodies leaning toward a single point between them; nothing else in the frame

17.subject: a small figure from behind holding a second glyph-form that is visibly disintegrating into loose fragments at its edges
17.geometry: show the danger of the idea or the image reads as an advertisement; decay at the edges, figure calm and small

18.subject: a single large eye-form with exactly four pupils, each pupil showing a different horizontal band of the same scene
18.geometry: extra eyes mean extra perception; each pupil a different spectral band, cyan and magenta only

19.subject: a glowing ring of light around a hole of absolute pure black shaped like a standing person
19.geometry: pure black inside a glowing image is the loudest shape you can draw; the void must have no texture at all

20.subject: one ordinary rose, rendered with near-photographic shading in greyscale, sitting dead centre on a receding perspective grid
20.geometry: one familiar object done properly beats twelve invented ones; the frame is empty and confident around it

21.subject: six figures of different heights caught mid-action at the same instant, none of them posing, all of them facing east
21.geometry: a cast mid-action is a scene; keep every figure on a different diagonal so nothing reads as a lineup

22.subject: a caduceus and a double helix standing side by side at equal height, sharing one base
22.geometry: use symbols people already recognise; the two must be drawn to the same standard of finish so neither wins

23.subject: an entirely ornamental panel of interlaced crimson and gold filigree with nothing depicted inside it at all
23.geometry: beauty with no information still has value; the composition must be beautiful enough that the emptiness reads as a choice

24.subject: an empty engraved book plate: a gold double-ruled border with corner ornaments and a completely blank cartouche at its centre
24.geometry: a frame waiting for a name that has not been chosen; the blank centre is the subject, not an oversight

25.subject: a laboratory instrument built from concentric dials and a sweeping needle, every scale marked in strokes that only look like numbers
25.geometry: it must look like real equipment; each label is noise, so mark scales with tick strokes and never glyphs

26.subject: eight identical circular subsystems on a ring around one empty core, connected by thin radial spokes
26.geometry: use the layout and write the labels yourself afterwards; leave every node face blank

27.subject: a nine-cell system diagram with correct structure and crude execution: flat mustard fills, thick clumsy outlines, no finesse anywhere
27.geometry: a bad-looking image can still carry the right structure; do not improve on it

28.subject: an assembly diagram where rectangular badge callouts point at clean empty white space
28.geometry: badge callouts pointing at nothing: asked to name, failed to name; leader lines must land on empty boxes

29.subject: a single polyhedron with exactly eight wheels arranged around it, drawn as pure line-work on a dark ground
29.geometry: the empty version is the most reusable version; nothing else in the frame, no key, no legend, no title block

30.subject: an engraved book plate with a heavy gold border, its blank centre now carrying a single crisp line of capital lettering
30.geometry: the one word this series ever spelled correctly; the lettering must be clean, centred, and the only text in the image

31.subject: a colour key: eight colour swatches in a numbered column beside the eight-node ring diagram they belong to
31.geometry: a numbered colour-keyed legend is the thing to copy; keep swatch, index mark and node aligned on one grid

32.subject: an ornate violet-and-gold filigree panel so beautiful that a viewer cannot tell what it is meant to depict
32.geometry: beautiful and uninformative: the trap of good taste; no focal object, no figure, no ground plane

33.subject: a finished comic page in three rows of panels, cream paper and black ink with one magenta accent, reading left to right: a whirl, a hand, a small figure, then a tunnel
33.geometry: a real panel grid, a real colour script and one real beat sequence; this is the only image in the series that is already a page

34.subject: a small hooded figure from behind, alone at the bottom of an empty cream-white field, with a single magenta eye-form placed exactly above its head
34.geometry: inverted ground: pale paper instead of black; align the symbol exactly with the head so the pair becomes one statement
34.ground: invert the register's usual ground: cream-white paper instead of near-black, with the magenta as the only ink

35.subject: a tall column of small chevrons stacked upward, and every single chevron points east
35.geometry: the axis is vertical but every road segment points east, so rule one is visible rather than violated

36.subject: two overlapping outlined triangles, upright and inverted, sharing one vertex — seven points where geometry only allows six
36.geometry: the seventh point must land off-axis and read as wrong; hold the frame still and empty around it

37.subject: an empty tailored suit on a hanger, its own hood-shaped void where a head would be
37.geometry: the cleanest line-work in the set: fewer strokes than any other cover, one confident contour per edge

38.subject: a hooded figure from behind so close it fills the frame, the hood a solid black mass with a single thin red rim light
38.geometry: focal hierarchy beats detail: one dominant shape, no secondary objects, no background incident

39.subject: a single large green eye low in the frame, looking down a corridor of blue walls lit by orange lamps
39.geometry: blue and orange is the strongest pair for power; the green is the only third colour and appears nowhere else

40.subject: the whole composition reduced to one crimson ink on cream paper: a road running east toward one standing figure
40.geometry: strip it to a single hue and it gains value; no second ink anywhere, all separation carried by line weight and dot density

41.subject: an empty page frame: one amber rectangle, one inner margin rule, four corner crop marks, nothing inside
41.geometry: generate the empty frame, never the labelled one; pure geometry, zero text, nothing placed in the field

42.subject: a complete infographic sheet — title band, year, subtitle, section headers, a topology diagram, a legend and a paragraph of body copy — where the layout is entirely correct and every word is wrong
42.geometry: real chrome, wrong words: the whole infographic survives on layout alone

43.subject: a node-link graph of thirty nodes in three distinct shapes and three colours, laid out by a force simulation, one library name printed small in the corner
43.geometry: it knows the tool it is imitating; let the layout be slightly untidy so it reads as generated rather than designed

44.subject: an engineering blueprint sheet: nine stacked layers drawn in cross-section, with dimension rules, leader lines, tick-marked scales and a title block
44.geometry: dials, leader lines and dimension rules are the layout grammar of a real sheet; keep every rule thin, straight and parallel

45.subject: nine figures of the same build caught mid-gesture at nine different stages, layered front to back in one frame
45.geometry: figures mid-action is a scene you can describe; stagger them on a single diagonal so all nine read separately

46.subject: a tall narrow stack of five slabs rising from a base, and one small shape perched on the very top
46.geometry: a vertical stack with something perched on top is a spine; nothing else in the frame, no ground, no horizon

47.subject: a tree trunk whose bark resolves into a single calm face, wearing a thin halo of gold rays at the crown
47.geometry: bark as face plus a halo crown equals authority; the face must be formed from the bark texture, never drawn on top of it

48.subject: one symmetrical being at the exact centre, crowned in fire, absolutely still, its left half cyan and its right half magenta-gold
48.geometry: perfect symmetry, dead centre, no motion at all; this is the cover that states the thesis and must feel final
